title: Identification in Finite DAGs with Unknown Deterministic Hidden Mechanisms and Structural Zeros
banked_reason: D0.5 panels pass, but achieved subfield tier is below the field floor; paper score ceiling 6.5 < 7.4 and no bounded same-topic repair lifts the contribution.
gap_reasons: Its claim of an implementable compiler is supported by a finite Bell-number bound and one diamond-family census, but no maintained general-alphabet implementation or evidence of performance across graphs is delivered.
The diamond result establishes a representation count, not a solver or asymptotic advantage over the linear-size factorized formulation, as the framing correctly acknowledges.

[D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a complete exact-law/support test for the fixed-alphabet deterministic-hidden class, cross-branch fibers and rational twins, and a sharp bottleneck identified set. A strict-positivity domain error and a staged-tree/CEG positioning omission were repaired and both D0.5 panels passed without findings. The field target failed because the representation count did not beat a linear-size factorized baseline and the package lacked a maintained general-alphabet implementation and performance evidence; the achieved tier was subfield.
tldr: For a finite fixed-alphabet DAG with unknown deterministic hidden maps, the theorem chain compiles attainable observed-history signatures and tests exact-support common-law fibers by sparse polynomial identities, producing guarded formulas or rational twins. The serial diamond family has eight signatures, at most 22 compiler states per layer, and exactly \(87\ell-58\) transitions; a faithful factorized response-function program also has linear size, so these counts make no solver-complexity separation claim. A separate bottleneck result characterizes when observed outcome profiles identify an event despite missing treatment overlap.
gap: Positive-law CSI identification handles supplied label systems, while general polynomial programming gives sharp bounds; neither verified result supplies a fixed-alphabet hidden-map union with complete exact-support branch-pair tests. Structural zeros make unreached row freedom and cross-branch equality decisive.
fill: Prove simultaneous partition realization, a bounded-frontier compiler and named direct-encoding separation, exact common-mask pair fibers with same-signature private rows, sparse supportwise and pointwise identity tests, and the bottleneck profile-capacity boundary.
